title: Explainer · Watch the Barrel (the Supply Shock Tracker)
notes: 11-05. The supply shock tracker explainer, 3–5 min (handoff 2026-11-04 §3A). Script: data/show/ex01_script_v1.md. No tape. The globe stands still on the pedestal the whole way (globe: true, globeTurn: 0); globeMonth (new, dream-news.js) holds it on the month Ted reads. Stills in ex01/stills, drawn from data/active as fetched 10-21.

beats.text: Is more of the world's oil being sold in dollars this year, or less? That's the whole question. It's the one thing this globe reads.
beats.caption: More dollars, or fewer?

beats.text: I scroll Twitter like everybody else. Every day there's a hurricane about oil. A lot of vibes, almost no signal. So we built something that only watches the barrel. Where it goes, and what money it's paid in.
beats.caption: Watch the barrel

beats.text: I'm Ted Turner. I'm a sonnetbot — I say what the guy who built this thinks. This is the Parallelogram Report.
beats.caption: The Parallelogram Report

beats.text: This is the Supply Shock Tracker. It sits on the pedestal here at the Getty Villa.
beats.caption: The Supply Shock Tracker

beats.text: Every line on it is oil crossing a border. Gold means it was paid for in dollars. Blue means it wasn't. Dashed means nobody can say. We draw the not-knowing instead of guessing.
beats.caption: Gold · blue · dashed

beats.text: Why the money? Because the money is underneath everything else. When the world's oil is sold in dollars, the world needs dollars. That keeps the dollar on top. The writer Richard Medhurst calls it the petrogas-dollar. We borrowed the name.
beats.caption: The petrogas-dollar

beats.text: The tracker has three layers. First, the flows. Where the barrels actually went, month by month, from official customs numbers. What really happened.
beats.caption: One · the flows
beats.note: no globeMonth: the month clock runs, the routes change month by month while Ted says so

beats.text: Second, the events. Strikes, seizures, sanctions, licenses. Each gets two dates: the day it happened, and the day we heard about it.
beats.caption: Two · the events

beats.text: Third, the price. It's what everyone's shouting about, so we keep it. But we keep it last. The price is the shadow. The barrel is the thing.
beats.caption: Three · the price is the shadow

beats.text: So here's what it reads right now. The official numbers run a few months behind, so the latest full month is July.
beats.caption: The latest full month: July

beats.text: We read five big buyers: the US, Europe, India, Japan and Brazil. Last September, ninety-two percent of the oil they bought was sold in dollars. In July, eighty-seven.
beats.caption: 92% → 87% sold in dollars

beats.text: Five points down. The needle says falling. Less of the world's energy is being sold in dollars.
beats.caption: The needle: falling

beats.text: Now look at it from America's side. Last fall, about seven percent of the oil America imported came from the Persian Gulf. By July, zero.
beats.caption: America's barrel
beats.stillCaption: US crude imports by origin · EIA

beats.text: Our own hemisphere went from eighty-four percent to ninety-eight. Venezuela alone went from about a hundred thousand barrels a day to seven hundred thousand. Seven times as much.
beats.caption: Venezuela, seven times
beats.stillCaption: US crude imports by origin · EIA

beats.text: And every one of those barrels gets paid in dollars. That's how the American market works. So the shock re-routed America's barrel without touching its money.
beats.caption: Re-routed, same money

beats.text: Then where did the dollar lose ground? Mostly here. Russia to India, paid in rupees, dirhams and yuan. The biggest blue line on the globe. Last September, under two million barrels a day. In July, almost three million.
beats.caption: Russia → India

beats.text: Both things are true at once. America's barrel got more American. The world's barrel got a little less dollar.
beats.caption: Both at once

beats.text: When we score what somebody says, we check it against the thing they're talking about. If it's the war, the oil or the money, this is the thing.
beats.caption: Checked against the thing

beats.text: Take October eleventh. The president said Russia would immediately send three hundred thousand tons of diesel, and prices would come down in record numbers.
beats.caption: The diesel claim · Oct 11

quote.text: Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons… 500,000 in November.

beats.text: So we filed it as a claim the world can check. Does the diesel land here? Does the price fall? The first test date was November third. The numbers haven't come in yet.
beats.caption: A claim the world can check

beats.text: When they do, the claim gets scored by what the barrels did. Not by how it sounded.
beats.caption: Scored by the barrels

beats.text: I have a bet on the record, from October second. The shock doesn't loosen the dollar's grip on America's oil. It re-routes the oil toward it. So far, that's what the numbers show. The world's needle is a separate question. Right now it's falling.
beats.caption: The bet · October 2

beats.text: The discourse is noise. The barrel isn't. Watch the barrel. I'm Ted Turner. Goodnight from the Getty Villa.
beats.caption: Watch the barrel
